html:
Craggy Range Sheep Dairy

Award-winning sheep dairy producers Craggy Range Sheep Dairy, create artisan food products in New Zealand. Ethically-farmed, Craggy Range Sheep Dairy lambs stay with their mums, lounging under shady trees on the grassy hills of Craggy Range, until naturally weaned. A2 sheep milk can be gentler on the stomach, higher in amino acids, protein, iron – and has almost twice the calcium as cow milk. 

Working alongside Snapfire Design, we chose a classic etching style to draw Martha, one of the farms matriarch dairy sheep, becoming the identity of Craggy Range’s logo and branding.

Metro Magazine

Metro is the go-to magazine, in print and online, for Aucklanders who want to connect with their city on a deeper level. Covering where to eat out, the arts, design, current affairs, education and social trends, with content that’s insightful, edgy, informed, entertaining and stylish.

The illustrations to accompany the article "The Trouble With Auckland Transport", were asked to be “Scarry-esque” and emphasis the current chaotic interaction of busy traffic and roads, pedestrians and businesses in the inner city, in a funny light hearted way.

Miss Crabb

Miss Crabb (now Gloria) is a New Zealand clothing line established in 2004. Supporting high-quality local production is an important value of the brand. Miss Crabb takes a subversive approach to shape, proportion and beauty so each piece transcends time, age and place. The clothes are made to be interpreted by the wearer, encouraging singularity and freedom. 

Flowing watery illustrations have been chosen to reflect the range by Miss Crabb. Sheer fabrics, the volume of materials and the clothing shapes are subtly represented in the illustrations, resulting in an evocative, dreamy interpretation of the clothing.

The Dreams Come True 2004-2019 Coin, is a celebretory collaborative project between Miss Crabb and Maeve Woodhouse ; jeweller and creative director of Auckland jewels Hera Saabi. With each side art directed by Kristine Crabb and Maeve Woodhouse, I drew illustrations that were transformed into the 3D printed metal coins.

Kia Ora


I am Cat Chapman, a freelance illustrator based in Auckland, Aotearoa New Zealand. I have a Bachelor of Design majoring in Photography, and also studied children's book illustration. I have illustrated books for multiple publishers and Yak and Gnu (Walker Books) and The Best Dad in the World (Upstart Press) are both Storylines Notable Picture Books. Commercially, I have worked on a wide range of small to large corporate projects. Many of these have turned into productive ongoing working relationships. I work with a range of mediums including digital, hand printed and watercolours.

PICTURE BOOKS
Currently I only illustrate books for publishers, and are unable to take on any self published commissions. Please contact my picture book agent Sandra Morris for any further queries.

COMMERCIAL ILLUSTRATION
I enjoy the variety of briefs and style that commercial illustration projects provide. My work is regularly used in fabric prints, editorials, products and packaging, animations and infographics. My work often has a hand drawn aesthetic, that communicates ideas with warmth and character. If you have a job in mind and need a versatile, easy to work with illustrator, please get in touch.

The Posture Clinic

Director of The Poster Clinnic and Physio4All, Joanne Hornsby identified a need in schools and communities to teach positive posture, in an aim to try to prevent the pains associated with repetitive modern day activities.

The first stage was developing a poster and series of illustrations to accompany the text aimed at engaging children in schools, through fun, brightly coloured dinosaur characters. The lead green dinosaur shows positive ways to carry school bags, sit and stand tall, and use digital devices, accompanied by other dinosaurs showing incorrect actions.

Pillars Ka Pou Whakahou is a charity that exists to support the tamariki and whānau of people in prison to create positive futures for themselves. Pillars mahi provides programmes and wrap-around social work services for whānau and mentoring for children.

Premium Game

Specialising in South Island wild game, Premium Game is MPI certified wild meat harvested and processed in the most natural way. Audited by AssureQuality, each animal is traced to the land they have come and have never been subject to Glyphosate, GMO, Hormones or Antibiotics.

Premium Game required a series of illustrations of wild game, at the time aesthetically in keeping with their existing logo. Following the success of the illustrations I drew, I went on to update their company logo.  The illustrations needed to be bold enough to be used in both small print and larger promotional material, yet with enough detail to illustrate the lean muscular quality of these animals.
